$comment: SHRINK-ONLY baseline for scripts/check-reachable-advisories.mjs (plan
security-boundary-remediation-and-usability-2026-09-04, P-007).
`accepted` is the flat list the analyzer reads: a shipping high/critical advisory
listed here does not fail --strict. `entries` carries the REASON for each, which is
the part a reviewer needs and the derivation cannot supply.
This list may only SHRINK. Fixing an advisory removes its entry (the gate reports a
still-listed-but-resolved entry as STALE). A NEW shipping high/critical advisory must
be patched, not appended — appending is how a gate becomes a parking lot. Re-seed only
from `node scripts/check-reachable-advisories.mjs --list`, never from a hand grep.
Seeded 2026-09-05 from a measured run: 99 total advisories, 9 gating, 22 non-shipping
only, 12 unattributed (failed closed as shipping). RE-MEASURED 2026-09-05 after the
lodash-es fix landed: 93 total, 8 gating, 22 non-shipping only, 7 unattributed,
8 baselined, 0 NEW offenders, 0 stale.
Dispositions are now 8 deferred-semver-major and ZERO patch-eligible: the single
patch-eligible entry (lodash-es) was FIXED on 2026-09-05 and removed from this list,
which is what shrink-only looks like in practice. The split was corrected
TWICE on 2026-09-05, by two different failures of the same optimism:
(1) `npm audit --omit=dev` is OPTIMISTIC about fixes and called style-dictionary
patch-compatible when the installed tree required a major bump, so the analyzer
now reads fix feasibility from both lenses and takes the pessimistic one.
(2) That two-lens reconciliation only bites when npm returns fixAvailable as an
OBJECT carrying isSemVerMajor. When npm returns the BARE BOOLEAN `true` there is
no version to compare and BOTH lenses read patch-compatible — so the optimism
came straight back through a different door. Re-measured against the published
registry the same day: of the four then marked patch-eligible, only lodash-es
(4.17.21 -> 4.18.1) is genuinely semver-compatible. The other three each require
a breaking bump, which the ADVISORY RANGE alone proves without any manifest read:
`^<installed>` is a semver SUBSET of the vulnerable range, so no compatible
version escapes it. See each entry's reason for its measurement.
lodash-es has SINCE BEEN FIXED (root `overrides` pin to ^4.18.1 + install:safe,
2026-09-05) and is no longer in this list. The paragraph above is kept as the
reason the derivation exists, not as a description of an open entry.
That derivation IS NOW IMPLEMENTED (deriveFixFeasibility, WI-2144851): the
analyzer computes semver.subset('^' + installed, advisory range) per finding and
a lens saying `true` can no longer make a finding patch-compatible on its own.
HOW THESE DISPOSITIONS ARE MAINTAINED NOW — read this before editing one.
The stored `disposition` stays CURATED and the derivation POLICES it (rung 2 of
CLAUDE.md's derived-truth ladder, not rung 1). The reason is narrow: the derivation
reads the PROD `npm ls` tree, so an advisory whose only vulnerable copy is genuinely
dev-reachable is invisible to it, and a blind re-seed would DOWNGRADE a correct human
judgment to `undetermined`.
⚠ RETRACTED 2026-09-05: this paragraph used to cite langsmith as the measured example
of that blind spot, claiming its 0.3.87 copy was dev-reachable only. THAT WAS FALSE and
it was load-bearing — it is why nobody looked. @browserbasehq/stagehand is a PROD
`dependencies` entry of apps/operator (dev=false), and langsmith 0.3.87 sits in the
--omit=dev tree at testing-shell -> stagehand -> @langchain/core. The derivation could
not see it because of a bug in OUR collector, not a limit of the instrument:
collectInstalledVersions guarded its walk on a global `name@version` key, and npm ls
emits a workspace both as a bare dedupe stub and once in full — so meeting the stub
first skipped the populated node and dropped that whole subtree. Fixed by guarding on
node identity. langsmith now reports CORROBORATED.
The lesson worth keeping: an UNCORROBORATED row is a claim about OUR instrument, so
treat it as a bug report against this analyzer until proven otherwise. Writing down
'expect this to stay uncorroborated, correctly' converts a fixable defect into
permanent policy, and a fail-OPEN one reads as reassurance while it does so.
So the gate reports two different things, and they must not be conflated:
ADVISORY_DISPOSITION_DRIFT — the derivation measured and DISAGREES. Re-adjudicate the
entry; never edit the derivation to agree with it.
UNCORROBORATED — the derivation could not measure. The entry stands; this is a gap in
the instrument, never evidence against a curated reason.
Re-seed from `--list`, which now prints the derived disposition and the range it was
derived from beside each row.
RE-MEASURED 2026-10-01 (frozen-repair lint:reachable-advisories red): 68 total, 8 gating,
1 NEW offender (next, CRITICAL GHSA-vcvr-r3jv-pc5j, >=16.2.0 <16.3.6) — PATCHED by
next 16.3.4 -> 16.3.8 in package-lock.json, not baselined. js-yaml was re-adjudicated
to patch-eligible after ADVISORY_DISPOSITION_DRIFT (js-yaml 4.3.2 fixes it inside ^4.1.1).
⚠ The same morning's tree reported style-dictionary STALE and stagehand as drifted. Both
were ARTIFACTS: package-lock.json had drifted from the manifests (npm ls: invalid
@modelcontextprotocol/sdk, @anthropic-ai/sdk, …), and in that state `npm audit --omit=dev`
dropped style-dictionary's GHSA-vj5c-m527-mpff and reported stagehand's vulnerable range
narrower than it is. Once the lock was reconciled, both reverted, and their entries stand
unchanged. Judge STALE and drift only on a tree where `npm ls --omit=dev` is clean.
seededFrom: npm audit --omit=dev --json (reachability/severity) + npm audit --json (fix feasibility, tree as installed) + npm ls --omit=dev --all --json, attributed by workspace

@browserbasehq/stagehand.reason: Deferring the semver-major upgrade @browserbasehq/stagehand@3.4.0 -> 4.0.2 (latest published). CORRECTED 2026-09-05 from patch-eligible: npm returns the bare boolean fixAvailable:true, which the analyzer reads as patch-compatible, but the advisory range is `3.0.0 - 4.0.0-alpha-49bc5b68e4fbeb28a120b301b51c31a36db7d922` and apps/operator declares "^3.4.0" — `^3.4.0` is a semver SUBSET of that range (prereleases sort below 4.0.0), so no compatible 3.x escapes it. The bare `true` is npm saying it could fix the deps this package is vulnerable THROUGH (@langchain/core, puppeteer-core), not that stagehand itself has a compatible fix.

langsmith.reason: Deferring the breaking upgrade langsmith@0.3.87 -> 0.6.0+ (0.10.1 is latest published). CORRECTED 2026-09-05 from patch-eligible: the hoisted copy at node_modules/langsmith is 0.8.7 and is NOT vulnerable — the vulnerable copy is the one nested under @browserbasehq/stagehand at 0.3.87. The worst advisory (GHSA-3644-q5cj-c5c7, high) is fixed only at >=0.6.0, and `^0.3.87` is a semver SUBSET of `<0.6.0`; under 0.x semver a minor bump is breaking, so no compatible version escapes. Also blocked behind the stagehand entry: the vulnerable copy is stagehand's own pinned dependency, so a root override would force it inside a package that was never tested against it. This row now reports CORROBORATED. ⚠ RETRACTED 2026-09-05: it previously said 'EXPECT THIS ROW TO REPORT UNCORROBORATED, permanently and correctly', on the claim that the 0.3.87 copy was reachable only through a dev path. That was FALSE — stagehand is a PROD `dependencies` entry of apps/operator (dev=false) and 0.3.87 IS in the --omit=dev tree. The derivation could not see it because collectInstalledVersions keyed its cycle guard on `name@version` and npm ls emits a workspace both as a dedupe stub and once in full, so the populated subtree was skipped. That was a fail-OPEN bug in our own collector, now fixed by guarding on node identity. The disposition below was right all along and is now DERIVED-corroborated rather than merely asserted — but the instruction not to investigate was wrong, and is exactly why the bug survived.

style-dictionary.reason: Deferring the semver-major upgrade style-dictionary@4.4.0 -> 5.5.2 (latest published; the advisory's own fix floor is 5.4.4). Root declares "^4.4.0", which cannot reach either. RE-MEASURED 2026-09-05, later the same day: BOTH lenses now return the bare boolean fixAvailable:true — npm's advisory record moved from an isSemVerMajor object naming 5.5.2 to `>=4.3.0 <5.4.4` with no version attached — so the two-lens reconciliation that first corrected this entry no longer fires on it, and the analyzer currently reports it as patch-compatible. The disposition here is still right and is now derivable from the range alone: `^4.4.0` is a semver SUBSET of `>=4.3.0 <5.4.4`, so NO compatible version escapes. Do not re-file this as patch-eligible on the analyzer's say-so until that subset check is implemented.

d3.reason: Only fix is d3@7.9.0, a semver-major upgrade. P-007 explicitly excludes forced feature-removing upgrades, so this is deferred pending a compatibility assessment of the chart/graph surfaces.

d3-color.reason: Transitive via d3; same semver-major upgrade as d3. Resolves when d3 is assessed.

js-yaml.reason: RE-ADJUDICATED 2026-10-01 from deferred-semver-major after ADVISORY_DISPOSITION_DRIFT: the vulnerable range is now `4.0.0 - 4.3.1` (worst: GHSA-2883-xcg3-v3hh, <4.3.2) and js-yaml 4.3.2 is published. Every prod dependent of the single hoisted 4.1.1 copy (operator-core, astro, @astrojs/*) declares `^4.1.1`, so 4.3.2 is reachable without a breaking bump. The earlier reason (fix only via @mdxeditor/editor@4.2.3) no longer holds. Still accepted here only because the bump was kept out of the frozen-candidate repair that found the drift; patch it on staging and remove this entry.

markmap-view.reason: Only fix is markmap-view@0.18.12, semver-major. Deferred pending mindmap-rendering compatibility assessment.

nanoid.reason: Only fix routes through @excalidraw/excalidraw@0.17.6, semver-major. Deferred; excalidraw is a feature-bearing canvas surface.
